case.case_title: Velu Arasadevi v. Prematilaka and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [2004] 3 Sri L.R. 240

clause.text: No person shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner’s fundamental rights under Article 11 were infringed by the executive action of police/army personnel who raped her while on duty.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that she was raped by police/army personnel at a checkpoint, constituting a violation of her fundamental rights under Article 11.
key_facts: Petitioner was stopped at a checkpoint where the 1st and 2nd respondents were on duty.
Later, the 1st and 3rd respondents came to her home and ordered her to accompany them to the police station.
Instead of taking her to the police station, she was taken behind the checkpoint and raped by more than one person.
The petitioner was subjected to unlawful restraint on liberty.
Medical evidence was submitted confirming the rape.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 11 protects individuals from torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, and that rape by state agents while on duty constitutes such a violation.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Since the petitioner was raped by persons on duty at the checkpoint and unlawfully restrained, the State was responsible for the infringement of her fundamental rights under Article 11.
principles_established: State responsibility arises when fundamental rights are violated by executive action.
Rape by state agents constitutes cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment under Article 11.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s fundamental right under Article 11 was infringed by executive action and awarded compensation.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Compensation of Rs. 150,000 awarded to the petitioner payable by the State.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 11 was central to the court’s finding that the petitioner’s rape by state agents constituted a violation of her fundamental rights, leading to the award of compensation.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was raped by one or more persons near the checkpoint while they were on duty, constituting unlawful restraint and violation of fundamental rights under Article 11.
